acid: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability, the properties that keep database transactions reliable through crashes and power failures.
ad-hoc-query: An ad-hoc query is written on demand to answer a one-time business question rather than run on a schedule. Analysts lean on them for BI and data exploration.
agentic-ai: In agentic AI, models act as autonomous agents that plan, use tools, run complex workflows, and make decisions toward a goal without step-by-step human help.
aggregation: Aggregation groups many data values into one summary value such as a sum, average, or count. It is the basic operation behind most reports and KPI metrics.
ai-ism: An AI-ism is a cliched, repetitive, or sterile phrase typical of generic AI-generated text. Editorial best practice says to cut such phrases from final copy.
airflow: Apache Airflow is an open-source platform for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring workflows in code, with each pipeline defined as a DAG of dependent tasks.
alex-merced: Alex Merced is Head of Developer Relations at Dremio and an author and speaker on data lakehouses, Apache Iceberg, and Apache Polaris, with 77 books written.
analytics-engineer: Analytics engineers sit between data engineering and analysis, writing modular, tested SQL and dbt code that turns raw data into well-modeled tables for BI.
ann-approximate-nearest-neighbor: Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search finds vectors close to a query vector, giving up a little accuracy for large speed gains in big similarity searches.
anomaly-detection: Anomaly detection is the identification of rare items, events, or observations that raise suspicion because they differ sharply from the majority of the data.
apache-hudi: Apache Hudi is an open-source lakehouse table format that brings upserts, deletes, and incremental processing pipelines to data sitting in cloud object storage.
apache-iceberg: Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets. It lets Spark, Trino, Flink, and Dremio safely share one copy of data using SQL behavior.
apache-polaris: Apache Polaris is an open-source lakehouse catalog for Apache Iceberg, offering centralized access control, cross-engine credential vending, and multi-tenancy.
apache-spark: Apache Spark is an open-source distributed engine for batch, streaming, SQL, and machine learning work. In-memory computation is its edge over Hadoop MapReduce.
api-application-programming-interface: An API is a set of protocols and tools that lets software applications talk to each other, defining the methods and data formats used to request information.
api-gateway: An API gateway is the single entry point between clients and backend microservices, handling request routing, API composition, rate limits, and authentication.
artificial-intelligence: Artificial intelligence is the simulation of human intelligence by machines, covering learning from information, reasoning to conclusions, and self-correction.
athena: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service for analyzing data in Amazon S3 with standard SQL. There is no infrastructure to manage, and you pay per query run.
attention-mechanism: Attention is the Transformer component that lets a model focus on the most relevant parts of an input sequence as it generates output, for long-range context.
avro: Apache Avro is a row-oriented serialization system with a compact binary format and schemas written in JSON, a common fit for Kafka event streaming setups.
aws-amazon-web-services: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a cloud platform offering more than 200 services from data centers worldwide, including compute power, storage, and databases.
azure-blob-storage: Azure Blob Storage is Microsoft Azure's object storage service for very large amounts of unstructured text or binary data, often used in cloud-native analytics.
azure-microsoft-azure: Microsoft Azure is Microsoft's cloud computing platform, offering analytics, virtual machines, database management, and AI services tied into Microsoft systems.
backpropagation: Backpropagation trains neural networks by computing the loss gradient for each weight and passing errors backward from the output layer to adjust the weights.
base: BASE stands for Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency. Distributed databases use it to favor availability and scale over the immediacy of ACID.
batch-size: Batch size is a machine learning hyperparameter that sets how many training samples a model processes in one iteration before its parameters are updated.
bias-variance-tradeoff: The bias-variance tradeoff is the tension between error from wrong assumptions (bias) and error from sensitivity to noise in training data (variance).
bigquery: BigQuery is Google Cloud's fully managed, serverless enterprise data warehouse. It runs fast SQL queries over petabytes of data on Google's own infrastructure.
cache: A cache stores data temporarily so later requests for it are served faster. In databases and search engines, caching cuts query latency and lowers server load.
cdc-change-data-capture: Change data capture (CDC) tracks inserts, updates, and deletes in a database as they happen, so downstream systems can react to each change in real time.
cdn-content-delivery-network: A content delivery network (CDN) is a geographically spread set of servers that cache web assets close to users, cutting page load delays for internet content.
classification: Classification is a supervised machine learning task where a model assigns each incoming data point to one of a fixed set of discrete classes or labels.
clickhouse: ClickHouse is an open-source columnar database built for real-time analytics. It uses SQL and is tuned to process petabytes of data with very low latency.
cloud-storage: Cloud storage keeps data on the internet with a provider that runs the storage as a managed service, offering scale and durability without owning the hardware.
clustering: In databases, clustering organizes table storage by the values of one or more columns so related rows sit physically together and range queries run faster.
clustering-algorithm: A clustering algorithm is an unsupervised learning method that groups data points by a similarity metric. K-Means and DBSCAN are two examples of the type.
colocation: Colocation means placing compute, data engines, or storage resources in the same data center so that network latency between them stays as low as possible.
columnar-database: A columnar database stores tables by column rather than by row. For analytical (OLAP) queries this layout cuts disk I/O and compresses data more effectively.
compaction: Compaction reorganizes storage files in transactional data lakes and databases, merging many small files into fewer large ones and resolving deletes.
compaction-job: A compaction job is a scheduled worker process that rewrites the transactional log files behind a table so that queries against it execute faster.
compute-storage-separation: Compute-storage separation lets a data platform scale and pay for storage and query engines independently, which avoids resource contention and lowers costs.
computer-vision: Computer vision is the field of AI that trains machines to interpret the visual world. Deep learning models use digital images to identify and classify objects.
consensus-protocol: A consensus protocol lets multiple unreliable nodes in a distributed system agree on one data value or system state, giving reliability and fault tolerance.
context-window: The context window is the most tokens a large language model can handle in one prompt and response. A larger window lets the model reference longer documents.
copy-on-write: Copy-on-write never edits data files in place. Each write copies the original data, applies the change, and writes a new file, keeping transactions isolated.
cosine-similarity: Cosine similarity scores how alike two vectors are from the cosine of the angle between them. It is a standard measure in document similarity and vector search.
dag-directed-acyclic-graph: A directed acyclic graph (DAG) maps tasks and their dependencies as edges with no loops, so a workflow can run in a reliable, ordered sequence of steps.
dagster: Dagster is a cloud-native orchestrator for machine learning, analytics, and ETL that treats data assets as first-class objects and stresses local testing.
dashboard: A dashboard is a visual interface showing KPIs, metrics, and analytical data points that summarize how an organization or process is performing at a glance.
data-analyst: A data analyst collects, cleans, and statistically analyzes data to support business decisions, then shares results through reports and dashboards.
data-asset: A data asset is any structured or unstructured file, table, database, or dashboard that holds business value and is managed within an organization.
data-catalog: A data catalog is a metadata-driven inventory of an organization's data assets that helps data teams find, evaluate, and manage the datasets they need.
data-cube: A data cube is a multi-dimensional view of data used in business intelligence, letting users analyze the same figures by time, geography, or product line.
data-engineer: Data engineers design, build, test, and maintain the pipelines, warehouses, and architectures that keep data clean, reliable, and ready for analytics.
data-fabric: A data fabric connects and manages data across systems, clouds, and physical locations, relying on metadata to automate integration and access control.
data-federation: Data federation lets users query several separate data sources as if they were one database, without copying or physically moving any of the underlying data.
data-governance: Data governance is the set of practices and processes for formally managing an organization's data assets, covering security, privacy, compliance, and catalogs.
data-lake: A data lake is a central repository for structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data at any scale, typically built on top of cloud object storage.
data-lakehouse: A data lakehouse pairs the cheap, scalable object storage of a data lake with the ACID transactions and SQL performance of a data warehouse in one architecture.
data-lakehouse-catalog: A data lakehouse catalog is the software interface that tracks transaction log structures, namespaces, and metadata file locations across a lakehouse.
data-lineage: Data lineage traces data from its origin through each transformation to its final destination across systems and pipelines, aiding debugging and governance.
data-lineage-graph: A data lineage graph is a visual map showing where data columns originate, which transformation steps they pass through, and where they end up.
data-marketplace: A data marketplace is an online platform where organizations publish, sell, license, or buy standardized datasets and analytical products from other parties.
data-mesh: Data mesh is a decentralized architecture that organizes data by business domain instead of central pipelines, treating data as a product owned by domain teams.
data-modeling: Data modeling defines the structure, relationships, constraints, and formats of a database or warehouse so storage stays consistent and queries run well.
data-quality: Data quality is the measure of how accurate, complete, reliable, and relevant data is for business operations and for analytical decision-making.
data-refresh: A data refresh is the scheduled update of data warehouses, data marts, or dashboards with the latest records pulled from transactional source systems.
data-retention: Data retention covers the policies and technical settings that decide how long records and tables are kept in storage before they are deleted or archived.
data-scientist: A data scientist applies statistics, machine learning, and predictive modeling to solve complex business problems and uncover insights hidden in data.
data-sharing: Data sharing gives external partners or other departments secure access to database tables or lakehouse datasets without copying the underlying files to them.
data-silo: A data silo is an isolated pocket of data inside an organization that one department can reach while the rest of the company is cut off from it.
data-source: A data source is where data originates, such as a transactional database, application API, log file, or IoT sensor, before analytical engines import it.
data-sovereignty: Data sovereignty is the principle that digital data falls under the laws and governance structures of the country where that data is physically located.
data-steward: A data steward maintains the quality, metadata, and security policies of datasets, acting as the accountable custodian for the data assets in their care.
data-stewardship: Data stewardship is the operational responsibility for managing data assets: keeping quality high, cataloging metadata, and ensuring policy compliance.
data-transformation: Data transformation is the process of cleaning, converting, and formatting raw data into structured tables that are optimized for reporting and analysis.
data-virtualization: Data virtualization lets applications retrieve and manipulate data without knowing technical details such as its format or where it physically lives.
data-warehouse: A data warehouse is a centralized, highly structured repository built for business intelligence, analytical queries, and reporting across historical datasets.
database-index: A database index is a structured pointer table built on columns so value filters run faster. The tradeoff is the extra disk space the index consumes.
databricks: Databricks is a cloud data platform built on Apache Spark, Delta Lake, and MLflow, serving data engineering, collaborative data science, and business analytics.
dbt-data-build-tool: dbt (data build tool) is an open-source command-line tool for transforming warehouse data with SQL select statements, with version control and testing built in.
decoder: A decoder is the part of a sequence-to-sequence model like a Transformer that turns encoded representations into output token by token, as in text generation.
deep-learning: Deep learning is the branch of machine learning built on neural networks with many layers. It tackles hard problems in vision, language, and prediction tasks.
deep-neural-network: A deep neural network has multiple hidden layers between its input and output layers, and those stacked layers let it learn high-level features from data.
delta-lake: Delta Lake is an open-source table format created by Databricks that adds ACID transactions, scalable metadata, and unified streaming and batch to data lakes.
denormalization: Denormalization deliberately adds redundant data to a schema to speed up queries. Fewer complex table joins are needed when related values are stored together.
dimension-table: A dimension table holds descriptive attributes in a star schema, such as customer name or product category, used to filter and group metrics in fact tables.
distributed-database: A distributed database spreads its files across two or more physical sites, on one network or several, and is designed to scale out horizontally as data grows.
distributed-query: A distributed query is one that runs in parallel across multiple database instances or cluster computing nodes, with each node handling part of the work.
docker: Docker is an open-source platform that deploys applications in lightweight, portable containers so they behave the same in development, testing, and production.
dot-product: The dot product takes two equal-length sequences of numbers, usually vectors, and returns one number. Vector databases use it to measure vector alignment.
double-bracket-link: A double-bracket link is wiki-style syntax for linking to another page by its title. On this site those links become relative paths at build time.
dremio: Dremio is an open SQL lakehouse engine that queries data in place on S3, ADLS, and GCS object storage, using an Apache Arrow engine and a semantic layer.
duckdb: DuckDB is an open-source, embedded columnar database for analytical queries. Often called the SQLite for analytics, it runs in the host process with no server.
elt-extract-load-transform: ELT (extract, load, transform) loads raw source data straight into a target such as a data warehouse, then transforms it there using the target's compute.
embedding: An embedding represents words, documents, or images as dense numerical vectors in a high-dimensional space that captures their meaning and relationships.
embedding-layer: An embedding layer is the neural network layer that maps discrete tokens or categorical features to dense, low-dimensional vector representations.
embedding-model: An embedding model is a machine learning model trained to turn text, images, and other inputs into vector embeddings that preserve semantic relationships.
encoder: An encoder is the part of a neural network, such as a Transformer, that turns input data into a contextual vector representation a decoder can then interpret.
entity-resolution: Entity resolution identifies and links records across separate datasets that refer to the same real-world entity, such as one customer stored under several IDs.
epoch: An epoch is one complete pass of the entire training dataset through a machine learning model's training algorithm, from the first sample to the last.
etl-extract-transform-load: ETL (extract, transform, load) pulls data from source systems, cleans and transforms it on a staging server, then loads the result into a data warehouse.
execution-plan: An execution plan is the sequence of operations a query optimizer chooses to read or update data, listing indexes used, join algorithms, and execution costs.
exploratory-data-analysis-eda: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) summarizes a dataset's main statistical characteristics, often with plots and other visuals, before any formal modeling begins.
f1-score: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, folding both into one number that measures the accuracy of a binary classification model.
fact-table: A fact table sits at the center of a star schema, storing quantitative measurements (facts) alongside foreign keys that reference dimension tables.
false-negative: A false negative is a classification error where the model predicts the negative class for a data point that actually belongs to the positive class.
false-positive: A false positive is a classification error where the model predicts the positive class for a data point that actually belongs to the negative class.
feature-engineering: Feature engineering selects, manipulates, and transforms raw data into new, informative features that improve a machine learning model's predictions.
feature-selection: Feature selection is the preprocessing step of choosing the most informative variables to train a machine learning algorithm, leaving the rest out.
feature-store: A feature store is a central repository for storing and serving curated machine learning features, keeping offline training and online inference consistent.
feature-vector: A feature vector is an n-dimensional list of numerical features that describes one object. Machine learning models take feature vectors as their standard input.
federated-query-engine: A federated query engine such as Trino is a distributed SQL processor that runs one query across several external databases at once without copying their data.
few-shot-learning: Few-shot learning is a machine learning scenario in which a model is trained or prompted to perform a task using only a small number of examples.
fine-tuning: Fine-tuning takes a pre-trained machine learning model and trains it further on a smaller, task-specific dataset to adapt its abilities to a specialized domain.
fivetran: Fivetran is a managed ELT platform that loads data from SaaS apps, databases, and file stores into warehouses or lakehouses, using log-based CDC for updates.
flink-apache-flink: Apache Flink is an open-source distributed stream processing framework for continuous data streams, built for low latency, high throughput, and stateful events.
fully-connected-layer: A fully connected layer is a neural network layer in which every node links to every node in the preceding layer, so each output depends on all of the inputs.
gcp-google-cloud-platform: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is Google's suite of cloud services for infrastructure, analytics, storage, databases, and ML, on hardware Google uses itself.
generative-adversarial-network-gan: A generative adversarial network (GAN) pits two neural networks, a generator and a discriminator, against each other to produce realistic synthetic data.
generative-ai: Generative AI is the branch of AI that creates new text, images, code, and music, using models trained on massive datasets of existing human-made content.
glowmorphism: Glowmorphism is a visual design style built from neon highlights, glowing borders, and drop shadows over dark translucent backdrops for high-contrast UIs.
google-cloud-storage: Google Cloud Storage is Google Cloud Platform's object storage service, used for serving website content, holding backups, and storing large analytics files.
gpt-generative-pre-trained-transformer: GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) names a family of decoder-only transformer language models trained on huge text corpora for many text generation tasks.
gpu-graphics-processing-unit: A GPU (graphics processing unit) is a specialized circuit built for fast memory manipulation, now widely used to speed up model training and heavy vector math.
gradient-descent: Gradient descent minimizes a model's loss function by repeatedly nudging its weights in the direction of steepest descent until the error stops falling.
graph-database: A graph database is a NoSQL store that models data as nodes, edges, and properties, built for querying highly connected relationships such as social networks.
guardrails: Guardrails are safety filters on generative AI systems that block harmful inputs and toxic outputs, enforce policy compliance, and help reduce hallucinations.
heuristic: A heuristic is a practical rule of thumb for solving problems quickly rather than exhaustively. Query optimizers use them to draft initial query paths.
hidden-partitioning: Hidden partitioning is an Apache Iceberg feature that derives partition values from source columns, so queries get pruning without naming partition filters.
hive-metastore: The Hive Metastore is the traditional central metadata catalog of the Apache Hadoop ecosystem, storing table schemas and the directory paths of table data.
hnsw-hierarchical-navigable-small-world: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor algorithm using multi-layer graphs for fast high-dimensional search.
home: The Data & AI Wiki is a curated reference on data infrastructure, open table formats, semantic layers, and AI, with sections on people, vendors, tools, terms.
hot-tier: A hot tier is a high-performance storage tier for active data that is queried frequently. It is served from fast SSDs or in-memory caches to speed up access.
hyperparameter: A hyperparameter is a machine learning setting fixed before training starts, such as learning rate or batch size, that governs how the model learns from data.
iac-infrastructure-as-code: Infrastructure as code (IaC) provisions and manages servers, databases, and networks through machine-readable config files instead of manual, interactive tools.
iam-identity-and-access-management: Identity and access management (IAM) is the set of policies and tools ensuring the right people and systems get the right access to cloud resources.
iceberg-manifest: An Iceberg manifest is an Avro file in an Apache Iceberg table that lists individual data files and records file-level statistical bounds used for pruning.
iceberg-rest-catalog: The Iceberg REST Catalog is a standard REST API spec for managing Apache Iceberg tables, so query engines can safely exchange metadata with one catalog.
in-database-analytics: In-database analytics runs analytical algorithms and machine learning models inside the database engine itself, avoiding the delays of exporting data.
in-memory-database: An in-memory database keeps its data mainly in RAM instead of on disk, which makes reads and writes far faster than in a disk-bound database management system.
incremental-load: An incremental load is an ETL or ELT process that updates a target database with only the records new or changed since the last run, which saves time.
indexing: Indexing builds data structures on table columns so searches and filters run faster. The cost is extra storage plus added overhead every time data is written.
individuals: The Individuals section of Alex Merced's Data & AI Wiki indexes profiles of people who work in data and AI, beginning with a profile of Alex Merced.
inference: Inference is running a trained machine learning model on new, unseen data to produce predictions, classifications, or generated content. It follows training.
internet-of-things-iot-data: IoT data is the continuous stream of sensor readings, telemetry, and status updates produced by physical devices that are connected to the internet.
ivf-flat: IVF-Flat is an inverted file index for vector databases that groups vectors into clusters and searches only those whose centroids are nearest the query vector.
json-javascript-object-notation: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a lightweight, text-based format for exchanging data. People can read and write it easily, and machines parse it quickly.
k-means-clustering: K-means is an unsupervised clustering algorithm that splits data into K distinct clusters by assigning each point to its nearest centroid by Euclidean distance.
k-nearest-neighbors: K-nearest neighbors (KNN) is a non-parametric algorithm for classification and regression that labels a point by a vote or average of its closest neighbors.
kafka-apache-kafka: Apache Kafka is an open-source distributed event streaming platform used by thousands of companies for high-performance data pipelines and streaming analytics.
kafka-connect: Kafka Connect is the Apache Kafka component designed to simplify integration between Kafka topics and external data sources such as databases.
key-value-store: A key-value store is a simple NoSQL database built on an associative array (a map), storing data as a collection of unique keys each linked to a value.
kpi-key-performance-indicator: A key performance indicator (KPI) is a quantifiable measure used to evaluate how well an organization, employee, or project is meeting its objectives.
kubernetes: Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration system that automates deploying, scaling, and managing containerized apps across clusters of machines.
lakehouse-storage: Lakehouse storage is the open cloud object storage layer holding transactional Parquet or ORC tables that are managed by table formats like Apache Iceberg.
langchain: LangChain is an open-source framework for building applications on large language models, offering integrations, prompt templates, and chains of calls.
large-language-model: A large language model (LLM) is an AI model trained on massive text datasets to understand, generate, translate, and summarize human language across many tasks.
latent-space: Latent space is a compressed mathematical space where similar data points sit closer together, capturing hidden features of the original input data.
linear-regression: Linear regression is a basic supervised learning algorithm that models the relationship between dependent and independent variables by fitting a straight line.
llama: Llama is a family of open-source foundation large language models from Meta, widely used for running LLMs locally and as a base for custom fine-tuning projects.
llm-prompting: LLM prompting is the practice of sending context-rich instruction templates to large language models in order to shape the output that they generate.
load-balancer: A load balancer is a networking device or software that spreads incoming traffic across a group of backend servers to balance resource use and prevent overload.
logistic-regression: Logistic regression is a classification algorithm that predicts the probability of a binary outcome, such as yes or no, from a set of input features.
loss-function: A loss function measures the gap between a model's predictions and the actual target values during training, and that number guides model optimization.
manifest-file: In Apache Iceberg, a manifest file is an Avro file listing data or delete files with partition-level metrics, so engines can prune files at query planning.
manifest-list: In Apache Iceberg, a manifest list is an Avro file that tracks a snapshot's manifest files and their partition specs, enabling partition-level metadata pruning.
materialized-view: A materialized view stores a query's precomputed results physically on disk, so complex queries need not be re-evaluated. Several refresh strategies exist.
materialized-view-refresh: Materialized view refresh is the technique for keeping precalculated views in sync with incoming transactional writes so their stored results stay current.
merge-on-read: Merge-on-read is a write strategy that records updates and deletes in separate delete files, then merges them with the base data files when the data is read.
open-source: The Open Source Tools section of the Data & AI Wiki indexes open engines, table formats, catalogs, and orchestrators, from Apache Spark to Iceberg and Airflow.
project-nessie: Project Nessie is an open-source transactional catalog for Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake tables that adds Git-like branches, commits, merges, and tags.
shawn-gordon: Shawn Gordon is a Senior Developer Advocate at Collate, the company behind OpenMetadata, and a Grammy-nominated musician known for his educational content.
snowflake: Snowflake is a fully managed cloud data warehouse on AWS, GCP, and Azure that separates storage, compute, and services, running queries on virtual warehouses.
terms: The Data & AI Terms page is an alphabetical index of Alex Merced's wiki definitions for data, lakehouse, and AI concepts, from ACID to merge-on-read.
trino: Trino, formerly PrestoSQL, is an open-source distributed SQL engine for low-latency ad-hoc analytics that queries data in place and joins across systems.
vendor-platforms: The Vendor Platforms section of the Data & AI Wiki indexes commercial warehouse, lakehouse, integration, and observability platforms like Snowflake.
